method: Opened all ten chapter reference targets and inspected relevant passages. Legal fitness/speed/winter provisions also reuse same-day inspection from Chapter 6. Individual sign captions/artwork reuse the verified register with hash/dimension checks; not a claim that all six individual sign pages were fetched again.

sources.finding: Chapter 3 §§1, 14–15 and 68–72 supports fitness, visibility-based speed and lighting duties, including main-beam dazzle restrictions and fog-light combinations. Chapter 4 §10e supports the equipment-use limits; §§18a–18d confirms the winter-tyre framework for the ordinary light-vehicle case. Current provisions are used, not future amendments.

Confirms daytime running-light settings can leave rear/side lights off and may need manual correction in darkness, dawn/dusk or bad weather. An illuminated dashboard is not proof that the required exterior lights are on.

Inspected sections 4.2–4.3 of VTI report 980 hosted by Transportstyrelsen. Supports surface/vehicle effects on stopping, shared braking/cornering friction and ABS preserving lateral forces within the available friction. No road-design friction thresholds or braking-distance figures are imported as driver guarantees.

Confirms the ordinary light-vehicle 1 December–31 March condition-dependent requirement, 3 mm minimum, mountain/snowflake marking for studless car tyres, studded-use season and mixed-tyre restrictions. Supports car/trailer combinations and the winter-designed M+S light-trailer transition through 30 November 2028. Heavy-vehicle cases and exemptions remain separately scoped. Manuscript’s original 1 October check date is retained; these claims were rechecked on 5 October.
Confirms the 1.6 mm summer minimum, recommendation to fit the best-grip/deepest-tread tyres at the rear, and vehicle-instruction-based pressure checks.

Supports adapting speed and distance to the actual surface and recognising that tyre/assistance equipment does not replace suitable driving. No additional comparative tyre claims or accident statistics are introduced.

Confirms risk-training coverage of fatigue/risky behaviour and speed, safety and differing road/weather conditions, including skid training. The chapter directs practice to appropriate instruction rather than public-road experimentation.

Confirms both the hand-held use prohibition and the separate restriction on communication activities that adversely affect driving. Hands-free or mounted equipment does not remove the attention requirement.
Confirms starting rested, allowing time, adapting to conditions, keeping distance and taking regular breaks. No universal interval certifying fitness to continue is inferred.

Chapters 2–4 §3 and chapters 4–5 support reflection, trip timing/route/passenger choices, fatigue, personal motives and group pressure. The chapter’s qualitative replanning exercise does not claim a numerical risk model.

G7_sources.title: Winter Driving — Bridges Freeze First
G7_sources.version: Live safety page; date not displayed
G7_sources.locator: Bridges Freeze First, text and alt text
G7_sources.excerpt: the cold air surrounds the bridge both above and below
G7_sources.supports: Open air above/below bridge enables earlier freezing than nearby roads; slow before possible ice.
G7_sources.fallback_reason: TRV På glid? (21 November 2025) confirms exposed bridges cool quickly but does not explicitly teach above/below mechanism. TS/TRV/SMHI searches did not locate that full mechanism; NWS provides exact official explanation.
G7_sources.scope_limits: A bridge can freeze sooner, not a guarantee every bridge always freezes first; moisture, temperature and local conditions matter. No US winter casualty figures imported.

G7_sources.title: På glid? Nej! Så jobbar vi mot halka
G7_sources.locator: Kan det bli halt trots att det är plusgrader? Ishalka bullet; Du kan göra mycket själv items 1 and 4
G7_sources.excerpt: vägen ser våt ut snarare än hal
G7_sources.supports: Water freezes on an ice-cold road into deceptive ice; air may be above zero; rain near freezing calls for speed/space adaptation.
G7_sources.scope_limits: Road surface must be cold enough for freezing; near-zero air or rain alone does not prove ice. No salt-temperature or maintenance-performance claims imported. SMHI Trafikväder/Underkylt regn checked as corroboration only; TRV supports the teaching so no redundant SMHI citation added.
G7_sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

G7_sources.title: Arrive safely with these winter driving safety tips
G7_sources.locator: Reduce Your Speed, bullet beginning Slow down at the first sign of rain
G7_sources.excerpt: oil and dust have not washed away
G7_sources.supports: First rain after dry spell can be particularly slippery because accumulated oil/dust remain.
G7_sources.fallback_reason: Exact dry-spell/residue mechanism not located in TS/TRV inspected searches. UK Highway Code covers diesel spills/wet roads, not complete mechanism. Official county fire explanation selected.
G7_sources.scope_limits: Hazard explanation only. No US speed reductions, car-length following rules, lighting rules or chains instructions imported. Rain and residues can reduce grip; no fixed duration or claim rain later guarantees clean/safe road.
G7_sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

G7_sources.excerpt: Ett minskat väggrepp på bakhjulen i förhållande till framhjulen gör fordonet mer överstyrt.

G7_sources.title: Electronic Stability Control Systems — final-rule technical appendix
G7_sources.version: Docket NHTSA–2007–27662; 2007 prepublication final-rule PDF, 327 pages
G7_sources.locator: What NHTSA Means by Mitigating Excessive Understeer, Case 1, PDF/numbered p.310; Case 3 p.311
G7_sources.excerpt: how sharply the vehicle can turn is limited by the friction
G7_sources.supports: Front-axle saturation limits turn; further steering cannot tighten curve. Rear-first saturation produces rapid rear rotation.
G7_sources.fallback_reason: VTI report gives understeer path and axle-grip framework but not the explicit front-axle limit passage in plain detail. NHTSA appendix supplies exact front-contact mechanism.
G7_sources.scope_limits: Technical grip-limit explanation only; no US ESC compliance rules imported. Restricted to loss-of-grip understeer, not claim that every ordinarily understeering car has already lost grip.
G7_sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

G7_sources.version: Live official manual; update date not displayed
G7_sources.locator: Road Conditions — Hydroplaning, definition and response items 1–4
G7_sources.excerpt: Do not slam on the brakes or try to turn suddenly
G7_sources.supports: Water film disrupts tyre grip/contact; slowly release accelerator, avoid abrupt braking/steering; gradually contact returns.
G7_sources.fallback_reason: TS/TRV results and VTI friction report cover drainage/friction risk, but no exact full definition and driver response located. UK rule 227 supplies easing/slowing only; PennDOT provides full essential advice.
